# Wound care (stop bleeding, clean, tie vessels, leave dirty wounds open) (`wound_care`)

<!-- generated by scripts/build_techtree.py from techtree/core/medicine.yaml — do not edit -->

- Category: Medicine & hygiene (`medicine`)
- Deps: helped by heat_sterilisation, antiseptics, hand_hygiene, blood_circulation, anatomy_dissection
- Core idea: Use firm, continuous direct pressure to control bleeding and obtain urgent help for severe blood loss. Clean minor wounds with ample clean water and cover with a clean dressing. Deep, heavily contaminated or crushed wounds need skilled exploration and removal of dead tissue. Whether and when to close a wound depends on its condition, site and infection risk; a universal six-hour cut-off is unreliable. Leave embedded objects in place for skilled removal. Spreading redness, fever or pus warrants assessment. Ligatures, drainage and sutures were important surgical advances but each requires the appropriate skills and clean equipment.
- Pitfalls:
  - Cautery with hot iron or boiling oil, and pouring irritants into the wound
  - Sewing a dirty or deep stab wound shut, which breeds gangrene and lockjaw
  - Believing 'laudable pus' is needed for healing and provoking it
  - Dressings of cobweb, dung, earth or unwashed rags (tetanus)
  - A tourniquet left on for hours, or tied too loosely so that it only blocks the veins
- History: egypt: c. 1600 BC – Edwin Smith papyrus: stitching, splints, honey and grease on wounds; india: early centuries AD – Sushruta Samhita: sutures, drainage, reconstruction of the nose (dating disputed); rome: 1st c. AD – Celsus describes tying bleeding vessels and the signs of inflammation; islamic: c. 1000 – al-Zahrawi (Córdoba) illustrates instruments, gut sutures and ligatures; europe: 1267 – Theodoric of Lucca argues wounds should heal clean without pus; 1545 Paré replaces boiling oil with a mild dressing; 1564 Paré ties arteries in amputations; 1718 Petit's screw tourniquet; 1898 Friedrich studies early excision in experimental wounds; this did not establish a universal six-hour limit
- Read:
  - Ambroise Paré, La méthode de traicter les playes faictes par hacquebutes et aultres bastons à feu (1545)
  - Guido Majno, The Healing Hand: Man and Wound in the Ancient World (1975)
